summary.title: RxFunction Gateway Server Threat Model
summary.description: Baseline threat model for RxFunction Gateway Server using STRIDE framework. Covers authentication paths, device communication, firmware distribution, data flows, and cloud infrastructure. Identifies all threats without assuming controls as a foundation for risk-based remediation prioritization.

diagrams.title: Gateway Server System Overview
diagrams.placeholder: System-level threat model for Gateway Server showing major trust boundaries and data flows

data.name: AWS Cloud Trust Boundary
data.description: AWS cloud infrastructure boundary. All services run within VPC with security group controls. Device authentication via mTLS using IAR-provisioned certificates. Operator access via MS Entra ID SSO through OAuth2-Proxy.

data.name: AWS IoT Core
data.description: MQTT broker with mTLS device authentication. Manages device connections, certificate lifecycle, MQTT topic policies, and IoT Device Shadows for configuration management.

threats.title: Device Shadow State Poisoning
threats.description: Attacker with cloud access could push malicious shadow state updates causing inappropriate therapy configurations on device reconnection.
threats.mitigation: Shadow state validation, version control, rate limiting on updates, audit trail for all changes

threats.title: MQTT Topic Access Violation
threats.description: Misconfigured IoT policies could allow access to MQTT topics belonging to other patients, enabling cross-patient data access and command injection.
threats.mitigation: Strict topic naming convention, policy templates, automated validation, least privilege access

data.name: AWS Lambda Functions
data.description: Lambda functions for CBOR-to-JSON conversion, message routing, device shadow updates, and API integrations. Processes CCI data (non-PHI).

threats.title: Lambda Code Injection
threats.description: Malformed CBOR data could exploit parsing vulnerabilities allowing code execution within Lambda environment.
threats.mitigation: Input validation, safe parsing libraries, sandboxed execution, memory limits

threats.title: Lambda Function Event Flooding
threats.description: Excessive MQTT messages from compromised devices could trigger Lambda throttling blocking legitimate data processing.
threats.mitigation: Rate limiting at IoT Core, Lambda reserved concurrency, DLQ for failed messages

data.name: RxFunction Gateway Server
data.description: Primary backend business logic. Handles device management, fleet-based firmware distribution, data processing, operator portal API, and third-party integrations. Processes CCI data only (non-PHI).

threats.title: Container Escape to Cluster
threats.description: Container vulnerability allowing escape to K8S cluster with access to all secrets and services, leading to complete infrastructure compromise.
threats.mitigation: Pod security policies, minimal container images, vulnerability scanning, RBAC restrictions

threats.title: Third-Party API Key Compromise
threats.description: API keys/tokens exposed via environment variables, logs, or memory enabling unauthorized use of third-party services.
threats.mitigation: Secure credential storage, environment-based injection, credential rotation, access auditing

threats.title: Firmware Distribution Tampering
threats.description: Compromised server distributes malicious firmware to entire device fleet causing widespread compromise and therapy manipulation.
threats.mitigation: Firmware signing verification, multi-party approval, integrity monitoring, audit trails

data.name: AWS DocumentDB
data.description: Primary database storing device records, therapy history, configurations, enrollment data, firmware manifests, and audit logs. All data is CCI (anonymized via UUID only, non-PHI).

threats.title: NoSQL Injection on Patient Records
threats.description: NoSQL injection allows unauthorized access or modification of patient therapy data and configurations.
threats.mitigation: Parameterized queries, input validation, least privilege DB users, query logging and monitoring

threats.title: Database Backup Exposure
threats.description: Unencrypted database backups in S3 expose entire patient population therapy data and personal identifiers.
threats.mitigation: Encrypted backups, access logging, encryption key management, lifecycle policies

data.name: S3 Storage Buckets
data.description: IAR-signed firmware images (organized by fleet/hardware revision), log aggregation, and temporary file transfer via presigned URLs. All firmware verified by device Secure Boot Manager on download.

threats.title: Bucket Misconfiguration - Public Access
threats.description: Public S3 bucket exposes firmware images, therapy logs, or transfer files to unauthorized internet access.
threats.mitigation: Bucket policies, block public access, access logging, automated configuration scanning

threats.title: Firmware Poisoning Attack
threats.description: Attacker gaining S3 access replaces firmware with malicious versions, causing fleet-wide compromise through update mechanisms.
threats.mitigation: S3 versioning and locking, multi-party approval, prevent policy changes, monitor modifications

threats.title: Presigned URL Token Leakage
threats.description: Long-lived presigned URLs leaked in logs or error messages allowing unauthorized firmware downloads.
threats.mitigation: Short expiration times (15 minutes), URL usage monitoring, secure logging practices

data.name: Redis Cache
data.description: Session storage (OAuth2-Proxy sessions), pub/sub messaging within K8S cluster, and cache layer for frequently accessed device data. Session tokens are sensitive - compromise enables operator impersonation.

threats.title: Redis Session Key Tampering
threats.description: Unsecured Redis connection allows modification of session keys/values enabling operator privilege escalation.
threats.mitigation: Redis authentication, TLS encryption, session integrity checks, access restrictions

data.name: Gateways (LTE)
data.description: Fleet of patient home Gateway/Docking Stations connecting via LTE. Authenticate to IoT Core using mTLS with device identity certificates from IAR provisioning.

data.name: Web Portal Users
data.description: RxFunction staff (operators, clinicians, support) accessing management portal. Authenticated via MS Entra ID (Azure AD) SSO through OAuth2-Proxy.

data.name: Device Connections (MQTT/mTLS)
data.description: Gateway devices connect to IoT Core via MQTT over mTLS. Authentication via IAR-provisioned device certificates. Carries telemetry, device identifiers, shadow updates, and commands. No PHI transmitted - all data anonymized at source.

threats.title: MQTT Message Tampering
threats.description: Attacker intercepts and modifies MQTT messages causing corrupted telemetry or invalid device state.
threats.mitigation: Message authentication codes, data integrity validation, replay detection

data.name: Firmware Distribution (S3 Pre-signed URL)
data.description: Signed firmware delivered to gateways via S3 presigned HTTPS URLs with short TTL. Gateway Server stages firmware and issues time-limited download link. Device verifies firmware signature before installation.

threats.title: Presigned URL Replay Attack
threats.description: Attacker replays valid presigned URL within TTL to download firmware for reverse engineering or substitution.
threats.mitigation: Minimal TTL (15 min), single-use URLs where possible, usage audit logging, IP binding

data.name: Database Operations
data.description: Gateway Server reads/writes device records, configurations, therapy history, and audit logs to DocumentDB. All CCI (anonymized UUID-only, non-PHI).

threats.title: Connection String Exposure
threats.description: Database credentials leaked in logs or error messages enabling unauthorized database access.
threats.mitigation: Secure credential storage, connection string sanitization, structured logging without secrets
